Question Choices: A rigid transformation maps a segment of length 12 to its image. What is the image length?
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve distance.|The segment cannot stretch or shrink.
Solution: A rigid motion preserves the distance between the segment endpoints. The image length therefore equals the original length, 12.

Question Choices: A rigid transformation maps a 48-degree angle to its image. What is the image angle measure?
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve angle measures.|Turning or flipping does not change an angle.
Solution: Rigid motions preserve angle measure. The image angle has the same opening as the original, so it measures 48 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. Does a rigid transformation preserve area? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: The image has the same size and shape.|No scaling occurs.
Solution: Yes. A rigid motion preserves lengths and angles, so the image is congruent to the original. It covers the same area, although its position or orientation can change.

Question Choices: Triangle ABC maps to triangle DEF with A -> D, B -> E, C -> F. Which side corresponds to AB?
Hints: Match each endpoint using the mapping.|A maps to D and B maps to E.
Solution: Track both endpoints: A maps to D and B maps to E. Thus AB corresponds to DE, also named ED.

Question Choices: Select. Is a dilation with scale factor 2 a rigid transformation? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve lengths.|This dilation doubles lengths.
Solution: No. A rigid transformation preserves every distance. Multiplying a positive length by 2 changes it, so this dilation is not rigid.
